title: The Once and Future Queen
author: Joel Pollen
source: FFT Tutoring with the Lightning Squad (tutoring.fft.org.uk), screenshots supplied 6 Oct 2026

pages.heading: At the Lake
pages.text: Morgan stood at the edge of the lake and felt a shiver run through her. Even though it was early May, the air still had a winter chill and she could see her breath faintly in the early morning sun. The lake stretched out before her, calm and untouched by bird or beast. Nearby on the rocky shore, her loyal knights and closest friends were gathered, watching her silently. Her brother, Arthur, wrapped in his brown Druid’s robe smiled at her when she caught his eye and urged her forward with his thoughts. Morgan turned her attention back towards the lake and tried to ready herself. Somewhere out there in the icy water, was the object she had been sent to find.

pages.heading: A Warrior Mother
pages.text: Britain had been at war with itself for her entire life. Her earliest memories were of her mother, Igraine, strapping on her gleaming armour in her room at the top of the castle. Morgan would sit on the bed and watch in awe as her mother transformed herself from a kind, gentle lady of the house to a fearsome warrior, complete with sword and shield. Igraine kissed her goodbye every time she left for battle and Morgan would cry hot tears when she heard her mother’s horse storming across the drawbridge and into the countryside. Would she come back as she promised?

pages.heading: Lessons with Merlin
pages.text: When her mother was away at battle, Morgan and her brother, Arthur, were left in the care of the wise, old wizard, Merlin. From Merlin they learned many things: the names of the animals in the forest and birds in the sky; how to read and write and work with numbers; how to predict the movements of the stars, sun and moon, and how to handle a sword and bow, which Morgan liked best of all.

pages.heading: Struck Down
pages.text: Then one day, when Morgan was 12 and Arthur 10, her mother was struck down in battle by a poisoned arrow. Her knights fought bravely to pull her body from the enemy and bring her back to Cornwall, where her injuries could be nursed by Merlin and his magic. The wizard succeeded in stopping the poison from spreading further, thus saving Igraine’s life, but her legs were badly mangled, and she was told she would never walk again.

pages.heading: Stories by the Fire
pages.text: For months, Igraine shut herself up in her room at the top of the castle, forbidding even Morgan and Arthur from seeing her. Eventually, at Merlin’s pleading, she let the children in and in time grew sweet with them, even though Morgan could see the bitterness in her eyes. She knew her mother longed to be out in the field of battle, trying to unite the country and end the war. Some of Morgan’s fondest memories were the late nights she spent with Arthur in that room, listening to her mother’s stories, as the candle wax dripped and the fire in the hearth gradually dimmed.

pages.heading: The Legend of Excalibur
pages.text: Igraine would often tell them tales of the legendary sword, Excalibur, which only the true ruler of Britain could wield. The story goes that the sword was lost long ago when Uther Pendragon, the last true king of Britain was killed in battle. His knights fought over the sword, and it fell into darkness. Some say it lies at the top of a tall mountain, high in the clouds, others at the bottom of a black lake guarded by a sea serpent. Igraine spent years searching for the sword, but whenever it seemed like she was getting close to finding it, a new battle would break out and she would be called away again to war.

pages.heading: The True Heir
pages.text: Igraine explained – and it seemed like she looked at Morgan directly when she said this – that only the true heir to the throne of Britain can find the sword and claim it as their own. It would remain hidden to everyone else, for Excalibur belonged only to the once and future rulers of the land.

pages.heading: A Promise
pages.text: When Morgan turned 15, Igraine came down with a fever and her health grew worse. After a long battle with illness, she passed away on the eve of the winter solstice. At her funeral, thousands of people from the surrounding villages and towns came to pay their respects to the woman who sought to end the never-ending war. Morgan stood over Igraine’s coffin, draped in black, and promised her mother that she would take up the quest to find the legendary sword, Excalibur, and finally bring peace to the land.

pages.heading: Into the Water
pages.text: That was three years ago, and now, after many promising leads and even more dead ends, Morgan had come to the shores of this rocky lake in northern Wales, hoping to find the sword out there in the dark water. She took a deep breath and tried to focus her thoughts on the task at hand. When she felt ready, she removed her leather tunic and riding boots, and handed them to Sir Kay, her trusted knight and cup-bearer. With one final look at Arthur (smiling as always), she waded forward into the water.

pages.heading: Swimming Out
pages.text: The ground under her feet was rocky at first but soon gave way to soft sand. She could see the bottom for a while before the water rose to her chest and she was forced to begin swimming. The icy water chilled her to the bone, but she kept swimming forward with fast, purposeful strokes. She was trying to reach the centre of the lake as quickly as possible - for that was where the sword was said to be.

pages.heading: The Middle of the Lake
pages.text: After several minutes, Morgan stopped to catch her breath and look back at the shore behind her. She was surprised by how far she had swum. Her companions were now small figures on the lonely shore, watching her nervously. She looked around and tried to work out her location in the lake and guessed that she was close to the middle but not quite there. She swam on until she began to tire. Deciding she was close enough to the centre, she took a deep breath and dived.

pages.heading: Deep Water
pages.text: She failed to locate the bottom on her first and second attempts but succeeded the third time when she pushed through the pain in her head and ringing in her ears. The lake had to be at least 20 feet deep. If Excalibur was at the bottom as she hoped, it would not be an easy task to bring it to the surface. Morgan tried to calm herself and slow down her breathing. She thought of Igraine, brushing her hair for her in front of the silver mirror in her bedroom. She had loved those rare moments when Igraine was not at battle, and she could instead be a mother to her and do all those motherly things that Morgan wanted most.

pages.heading: Nothing but Rocks
pages.text: As calm washed over her, Morgan took a deep breath and plunged beneath the surface. She reached the bottom quicker this time and began to feel around for the sword, but there was nothing but mossy rocks and sand. She tried opening her eyes, but the light was so weak she could only see the faint outlines of the largest rocks. Feeling herself start to get dizzy, she kicked for the surface and fresh air.

pages.heading: Doubt
pages.text: She did several more dives, but each time came across nothing but rocks and sand. There weren’t even any fish about. Maybe she wasn’t in the centre of the lake? Or maybe this wasn’t the right lake at all? Maybe the sword isn’t even in a lake? She tried to push the growing doubt from her mind. No, the sword must be here. Every clue led back to this lake. It can’t be anywhere else.

pages.heading: The Reeds
pages.text: Acting on instinct, Morgan decided to swim a bit further out towards the western portion of the lake. After a few minutes she reached a spot that seemed right to her. When she dived down, she saw that the bottom wasn’t as deep here, and her vision was better. She could stay underwater longer and cover more ground. There were plants here as well - great green patches of reeds that grew from the floor of the lake and concealed tiny schools of fish. Morgan’s pulse quickened as she sensed she was on to something. She pushed through a curtain of reeds and there in the centre of a small clearing, half-buried in the sand, was the object she had come to find.

pages.heading: The Inscription
pages.text: The light filtering down from the surface showed the unmistakable silver glint of a sword blade, and Morgan reached forward in excitement. She wrapped her hands around the hilt and braced her feet against the lakebed, expecting a struggle, but instead the sword slipped out of the sand easily, like a knife through butter. Morgan stared at it in astonishment. On the blade, as if written in fire, was the inscription: For the once and future queen.

pages.heading: Excalibur
pages.text: Morgan’s head broke the surface, and she gulped in greedy mouthfuls of air. She had been under a lot longer than she had thought and it took her a while to catch her breath again. The sword was in her hands, heavy and gleaming in the sunlight. Could it really be true? After all the years Igraine, and later Morgan, and not to mention the countless others before them, spent searching for it, could it really be that she had finally found the lost sword, Excalibur? Her mother’s words echoed in her mind: Only the true heir to the throne of Britain can find the sword and claim it as their own.

pages.heading: Back to Shore
pages.text: Morgan would think about the meaning of this later. For now, she tucked the sword securely in her belt and began to swim back. When she reached the pebbled shore, her knights rushed forward to meet her, but they drew back in amazement when she stood up fully and revealed the dripping sword hanging from her belt. A stunned silence swept over the beach. Morgan searched for the right words but before she could, one by one, each of her knights dropped to their knees and bowed their heads before her.

pages.heading: Arthur’s Dream
pages.text: Embarrassed, Morgan rushed forward and tried to pull them up, but they remained stubbornly kneeling with their heads down. Arthur appeared with a shawl and wrapped it around her, before giving her a big hug, and flashing that knowing smile of his. “You knew I would find it here, didn’t you?” said Morgan. “I had a dream that you would,” replied Arthur. “Mother would be proud.”

pages.heading: The Once and Future Queen
pages.text: Morgan could feel tears welling in her eyes, but before she could think any further, Arthur spun her around to face the knights who had risen from their knees. They all looked at her with the same expression of wild expectation. She drew Excalibur from her belt and brandished it triumphantly above her head. The sun’s rays struck the blade, creating a blinding flash that sent a jet of light across the countryside towards the warring lands in the east A great cheer went up, and the knights shouted in unison ‘Hail, Morgan, queen of Britain! Hail, Morgan, the once and future queen!”

glossary.shiver: A quick shake of the body, from cold or fear.
glossary.awe: A feeling of wonder mixed with respect, or a little fear.
glossary.fearsome: Frightening to look at or face.
glossary.companions: People you travel or spend time with.
glossary.unison: All together, at the same time.
